output.brief: The complaints look like a brake-fluid problem, not driver technique or the pads. All 11 Eastgate vans with soft-pedal reports had their brakes serviced at Northfield Motor Services during the bay closure. Northfield's fluid drum was contaminated with water. The two warranty vans tested had boiling points of 152°C and 149°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. Drivers who ran Upper Wend in other vans reported no problems, which argues against technique. The Tessaro pads were fitted at other garages too, without complaints. Upper Wend's long descents are what exposes the weak fluid. I'm fairly confident, but this rests on documents and two tested vans, not a direct test of the other 11. Do this week: take the 13 Northfield vans out of service, boiling-point test and renew their fluid from sealed stock, and check LK-209 before it returns. Stop the warnings and the blanket retraining, since they punish drivers who reported real faults. Ask Northfield why its 10 September warranty warning went unanswered. Pad changes can wait for a separate noise review.
